source_text: Οὐκοῦν ὁ τὸν ναὸν ἀτιμάζων, ἀτιμάζει τὸν ἐν τῷ ναῷ Κύριον· καὶ ὁ διαιρῶν τὸν Λόγον ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος, ἀθετεῖ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ἐν αὐ τῷ. Καὶ ἀσεβέστατοι δὲ Ἀρειομανῖται μὴ, ἐπειδὴ τὸ σῶμα κτιστόν ἐστι, νομιζέτωσαν καὶ τὸν Λόγον εἶναι κτίσμα, μηδὲ διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι τὸν Λόγον κτίσμα, διαβαλλέτωσαν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ. Θαυμάσαι γάρ ἐστιν αὐτῶν τὴν κακόνοιαν, ὅτι καὶ πάντα κυκῶσι καὶ φύρουσι, καὶ προφάσεις ἐφευρίσκουσιν, ἵνα μόνον τὸν κτίστην τοῖς κτίσμασι συναριθμήσωσιν. Ἀλλ' ἀκουέτωσαν· Εἰ κτίσμα ἦν ὁ Λόγος, οὐ προσελάμβανε τὸ κτιστὸν σῶμα, ἵνα αὐτὸ ζωοποιήσῃ. Ποία γὰρ τοῖς κτίσμασι παρὰ κτίσματος ἔσται βοήθεια, δεομέ νου καὶ αὐτοῦ σωτηρίας; Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ, κτίστης ὢν ὁ Λόγος, αὐτὸς δημιουργὸς γέγονε τῶν κτισμάτων· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων τὸ κτιστὸν αὐτὸς ἐνεδύσατο, ἵνα πάλιν αὐτὸς, ὡς κτίστης, ἀνακαινίσῃ, καὶ ἀνακτῆσαι τοῦτο δυνηθῇ. Κτίσμα δὲ ὑπὸ κτίσματος οὐκ ἄν ποτε σωθῇ, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ κτίσματος ἐκτίσθησαν τὰ κτίσματα, εἰ μὴ κτίστης ἦν ὁ Λόγος. Ὅθεν μὴ καταψευδέσθωσαν τῶν θείων Γραφῶν, μηδὲ σκανδαλιζέτωσαν τοὺς ἀκεραίους τῶν ἀδελφῶν· ἀλλ' εἰ μὲν βούλωνται, μεταγινωσκέτωσαν καὶ αὐτοὶ, καὶ μηκέτι τῇ κτίσει λατρευέτωσαν παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα τὰ πάντα Θεόν· ἐὰν δὲ ταῖς ἀσεβείαις αὐτῶν ἐμμένειν ἐθέλωσι, μόνοι τούτων ἐμφορείσθωσαν, καὶ τριζέτωσαν τοὺς ὀδόντας κατὰ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν τὸν διάβολον, ὅτι ἡ πίστις τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας, κτίστην οἶδε τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λό γον καὶ δημιουργὸν τῶν ἁπάντων, καὶ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι Ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν ἦν ὁ Λόγος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν· γενόμενον δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ἄνθρωπον διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν προσκυνοῦμεν, οὐχ ὡς ἴσον ἐν ἴσῳ γενόμενον τῷ σώματι, ἀλλ' ὡς Δεσπότην προσλαβόντα τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορφὴν, καὶ δημιουργὸν καὶ κτίστην ἐν κτίσματι γινόμενον, ἵν', ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἐλευθερώσας, τὸν κόσμον προσαγάγῃ τῷ Πατρὶ, καὶ εἰρηνοποιήσῃ τὰ πάντα, τὰ ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Οὕτω γὰρ καὶ τὴν πατρικὴν αὐ-τοῦ θεότητα ἐπιγινώσκομεν, καὶ τὴν ἔνσαρκον αὐτοῦ παρουσίαν προσκυνοῦμεν, κἂν Ἀρειομανῖται διαῤῥηγνύωσιν ἑαυτούς. Προσαγόρευε πάντας τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν. Ἐῤῥῶσθαί σε καὶ μνημονεύειν ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ εὐχόμεθα, ἀγαπητὲ καὶ ὡς ἀληθῶς ποθεινότατε, ἐὰν χρεία ᾖ ἀναγνωσθῆναι ταῦτα Ἱερακᾷ τῷ πρεσβυτέρῳ.
thought_title: The Word as Creator in the flesh
orientation: Athanasius is concluding his letter to Adelphius, warning the Arians not to dishonor the Lord's body or divide the Word from it, and affirming the Church's worship of the incarnate Creator.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the [one] dishonoring the temple, dishonors the Lord in the temple; and the [one] dividing the Word from the body, rejects the grace the [one] given to us in him. And most impious Ariomanites, not, since the body created is, let them think also the Word to be a creature, nor because of the not being the Word a creature, let them slander the body of him. For to marvel is [at] their evil-mindedness, because both all things they stir up and mix together, and pretexts they invent, in order that only the Creator with the creatures they may number together. But let them hear: If a creature was the Word, not would he have taken in addition the created body, in order that it he might make alive. For what to the creatures from a creature will be help, [it] needing also itself salvation? But since, Creator being the Word, himself maker has become of the creatures; because of this also at [the] consummation of the ages the created [thing] himself he put on, in order that again himself, as Creator, he might renew, and recover this [thing] he might be able. But a creature by a creature not ever would be saved, just as neither by a creature were created the creatures, if not Creator was the Word. Wherefore let them not speak falsely against the divine Scriptures, nor let them scandalize the simple [ones] of the brothers; but if indeed they are willing, let them change their mind also themselves, and no longer to the creation let them worship alongside the [one] having created all things God; but if in their impieties to remain they wish, alone with these [things] let them be filled, and let them gnash the teeth according to the father of them the devil, because the faith of the catholic Church, Creator knows the Word of God and maker of all things, and we know, that In [the] beginning indeed was the Word, and the Word was with God; and having become him also man because of our salvation we worship, not as [an] equal in [an] equal having become to the body, but as Lord having taken in addition the form of the slave, and maker and Creator in [a] creature becoming, in order that, in him all things having freed, the world he might bring to the Father, and might make peace [with] all things, the [things] in [the] heavens and the [things] upon the earth. For thus also the paternal divinity of him we recognize, and the enfleshed presence of him we worship, even if Ariomanites tear themselves apart. Greet all the [ones] loving the Lord of us Jesus Christ. To be strong you and to remember us in [the] Lord we pray, beloved and truly most longed-for, if need is to be read these [things] to Hieracas the elder.

choices.why: The source uses this polemical form rather than Ἀρειανοί; the glossary bans 'Ariomaniacs' for Ἀρειανοί but this is a different source term, so the literal form is kept.

choices.term: ἴσον ἐν ἴσῳ γενόμενον τῷ σώματι
choices.english: an equal thing becoming equal to the body
choices.why: ἴσον is neuter, 'an equal thing', not 'one equal'; the phrase denies that the Word became an equal thing in equality with the body, preserving the grammar.
rejected: one equal becoming equal to the body

choices.term: ἵνα μόνον τὸν κτίστην τοῖς κτίσμασι συναριθμήσωσιν
choices.english: only so that they may number the Creator among the creatures
choices.why: μόνον ('only') is retained to show their sole aim, as the source states.
rejected: so that they may number the Creator among the creatures

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Pauline phrase; 'servant' keeps the δοῦλος sense without importing 'slave' connotations that might distract.
The verb means to tear or burst asunder; the reflexive with ἑαυτούς is kept literally to convey the violent image.

choices.english: let them be filled with them
choices.why: The verb means to be filled or sated; the dative τούτων refers to their impieties, so the literal sense is kept.
rejected: let them have their fill of them

pass_b_english: Therefore the one who dishonors the temple dishonors the Lord who is in the temple; and the one who divides the Word from the body rejects the grace given to us in him. And let the most impious Ariomaniacs not suppose, because the body is created, that the Word is also a creature; nor, because the Word is not a creature, let them slander his body. For their malice is to be marveled at, because they stir up and confuse everything, and they invent pretexts only so that they may number the Creator among the creatures. But let them hear: If the Word were a creature, he would not have taken to himself the created body in order to make it alive. For what help will there be for creatures from a creature, when it itself also needs salvation? But since the Word, being Creator, himself became the maker of creatures, for this reason also at the consummation of the ages he himself put on the created body, so that again he himself, as Creator, might renew it and be able to win it back. A creature could never be saved by a creature, just as creatures were not created by a creature, unless the Word were Creator. Therefore let them not speak falsely against the divine Scriptures, nor scandalize the innocent among the brothers; but if they are willing, let them also repent, and no longer worship the creature alongside the God who created all things. But if they wish to remain in their impieties, let them alone be filled with them, and let them gnash their teeth according to their father the devil, because the faith of the catholic Church knows the Word of God as Creator and maker of all things, and we know that in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God (John 1:1); and when he became also man for our salvation, we worship him, not as an equal thing becoming equal to the body, but as Lord taking the form of the servant (Philippians 2:7), and as maker and Creator becoming in a creature, so that, having freed all things in him, he might bring the world to the Father and make peace for all things, whether in heaven or on earth (Colossians 1:20). For thus we also recognize his paternal divinity, and we worship his incarnate presence, even if the Ariomaniacs burst themselves apart. Greet all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ. We pray that you fare well and remember us to the Lord, beloved and truly most longed for, if there is need for these things to be read to Hieracas the presbyter.

last_rejected.quote: nor, because the Word is not a creature, let them slander his body
last_rejected.source_quote: μηδὲ διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι τὸν Λόγον κτίσμα, διαβαλλέτωσαν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: Source says 'let them not slander his body because the Word is not a creature'; English reverses the causal logic.
last_rejected.fix: nor let them slander his body because the Word is not a creature
last_rejected.ruling: Greek μηδὲ...διαβαλλέτωσαν is 'nor let them slander'; διὰ τὸ gives their motive/reason, not result. English causal logic is correct.

last_rejected.quote: and let them gnash their teeth according to their father the devil
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τριζέτωσαν τοὺς ὀδόντας κατὰ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν τὸν διάβολον
last_rejected.why: Source says 'gnash their teeth against their father the devil'; 'according to' loses the adversative sense of κατά.
last_rejected.fix: and let them gnash their teeth against their father the devil
last_rejected.ruling: κατὰ + accusative here means 'according to'/'after the pattern of' (cf. LXX usage); 'according to' is standard, not adversative.

last_rejected.quote: not as an equal thing becoming equal to the body
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς ἴσον ἐν ἴσῳ γενόμενον τῷ σώματι
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'not as an equal becoming equal to the body' (the Word), not 'equal thing'.
last_rejected.fix: not as an equal becoming equal to the body
last_rejected.ruling: ἴσον as 'equal thing' is within normal range; no meaning lost or reader misled.

last_rejected.why: ἀνακτῆσαι means 'recover, win back, restore'—but context demands 'renew' or 'restore' to match ἀνακαινίσῃ.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνακτῆσαι means 'recover/win back'; coordinate with ἀνακαινίσῃ, not redundant. No error.
